title: 2015 AMC 10B Problem 11
statement: Among the positive integers less than \(100,\) each of whose digits is a prime number, one is selected at random. What is the probability that the selected number is prime?

solutions.text:
The available digits are \(2,3,5,7\). There are \(4\) one-digit numbers and \(4^2=16\) two-digit numbers, for \(20\) total choices.

All \(4\) one-digit choices are prime. A two-digit prime cannot end in \(2\) or \(5\), so checking endings \(3\) and \(7\) gives the two-digit primes \(23,37,53,73\).

Thus \(8\) of the \(20\) choices are prime, and the probability is \(\frac{8}{20}=\frac25\).

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: List one-digit primes and two-digit numbers using only \(2,3,5,7\)
Two-digit primes ending in \(3\) or \(7\) must still pass divisibility tests
